idiom-31-q21.truthCondition: Sam and Alex always argue angrily over who gets the chair beside the window.
idiom-31-q21.correctReason: 正確句保留兩人「總是」為窗邊座位吵架的習慣；慣用語描述的是爭執，不是搶椅子的動作。

foils.text: Sam and Alex always fight like cat and dog over who sits by the door.
foils.reason: 「by the door」把爭議座位由窗邊改成門邊。

foils.text: Sam and Alex fought like cat and dog once over who sits by the window.
foils.reason: 「once」把總是發生的爭吵改成一次事件。

foils.text: Sam and Alex agree to take turns sitting by the window without arguing.
foils.reason: 「take turns ... without arguing」表示輪流而沒有爭吵，與原題的大叫大嚷相反。

idiom-31-q22.truthCondition: The coach separated Ryan and Luke because they argued fiercely about every decision.
idiom-31-q22.correctReason: 原題是爭吵在先、教練分開兩人在後；正確句保留了原因、結果及「每個決定」。

foils.text: The coach separated Ryan and Luke before they began fighting like cat and dog over any decision.
foils.reason: 「before they began」把分開兩人的時間移到爭吵之前；原題說教練因爭吵才把他們分開。

foils.text: The coach separated Ryan and Luke because they fought like cat and dog over one decision.
foils.reason: 「one decision」把每個決定都吵的模式縮成單一決定。

foils.text: The coach kept Ryan and Luke together because they agreed on every decision.
foils.reason: 這句把教練分開兩人改成讓他們留在一起，也把爭吵改成同意。

idiom-31-q23.truthCondition: Whenever their family chooses a restaurant, Cara and her brother argue angrily over where to eat.
idiom-31-q23.correctReason: 「Whenever」對應每次選餐廳；正確句保留卡拉與哥哥為用餐地點激烈爭執。

foils.text: Whenever the family chooses a restaurant, Cara and her brother fight like cat and dog over the bill.
foils.reason: 「over the bill」把爭議由去哪裏吃改成由誰付款。

foils.text: After the family has eaten, Cara and her brother fight like cat and dog about where they ate.
foils.reason: 「After ... eaten」把爭吵移到用餐後；原題說選餐廳時便會爭吵。

foils.text: Whenever the family chooses a restaurant, Cara and her brother quickly agree where to eat.
foils.reason: 「quickly agree」表示兩人迅速取得共識，與原題相反。

idiom-31-q24.truthCondition: The two cousins often argue fiercely over a simple joke, even on happy days.
idiom-31-q24.correctReason: 正確句保留「即使在愉快的日子」和「經常因一個簡單笑話」兩項反差與頻率。

foils.text: Even on happy days, the two cousins often fight like cat and dog over a serious insult.
foils.reason: 「a serious insult」把普通笑話改成嚴重侮辱，失去原題的小事引發激烈爭吵的反差。

foils.text: Only on unhappy days do the two cousins fight like cat and dog over a simple joke.
foils.reason: 「Only on unhappy days」否定了原題說連愉快日子也會爭吵。

foils.text: Even on happy days, the two cousins laugh together instead of arguing over a simple joke.
foils.reason: 這句說兩人一起歡笑而不爭吵，倒轉了原題的反應。

idiom-31-q25.truthCondition: Nina reported that she and her flatmate argued angrily every day throughout the previous week about heating.
idiom-31-q25.correctText: Nina told me that she and her flatmate had fought like cat and dog about the heating every day last week.
idiom-31-q25.correctZh: 妮娜告訴我，她和室友上星期每天都為暖氣而激烈爭吵。
idiom-31-q25.answerOverrideReason: Restores the source's exact every-day frequency within the preceding week; 'all week' alone need not mean every day. Canonical source answer remains unchanged.
idiom-31-q25.correctReason: 「every day last week」保留上星期每天爭吵的頻率；「about the heating」保留暖氣爭議。

foils.text: Nina told me that she and her flatmate had fought like cat and dog all week about the rent.
foils.reason: 「the rent」把爭議由暖氣改成租金。

foils.text: Nina told me that she and her flatmate had fought like cat and dog once last week about the heating.
foils.reason: 「once last week」把上星期每天的爭吵改成只吵一次。

foils.text: Nina told me that she and her flatmate had agreed about the heating all week.
foils.reason: 「had agreed」把整星期的激烈爭吵改成整星期達成共識。
